comments.comment: 4:52 No, the book absolutely does not say that. The Selfish Gene has nothing to do with human selfishness. The “selfish” in the title refers to the fact that genes are the fundamental unit of reproduction, not the individual. Individual organisms are merely carriers of genes that only care about their own survival, hence “selfish”. This point of view makes it easier to understand how certain traits evolved, like altruism, where genes for altruistic behaviour (e.g. rescuing a drowning person) manifest in the organism in such a way as to protect copies of themselves in others, hence ensuring their own reproductive success.
